dependency_ordered_snapshots.statement: Adopt the SI system of units for this framework, with the following quantity table and conventions; every symbol is a quantity of this framework and the laboratory structure is that of [[def-em-lab-geometry]]. (a) [Coordinates and constants] $x^0=ct$ and each spatial coordinate $x^i$ carries the metre (m); the time coordinate $t$ carries the second (s); the conversion constant $c>0$ carries m s$^{-1}$ and has the exact SI defining value $c=299\,792\,458\ \mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; the elementary charge $e$ has the exact SI defining value $e=1.602\,176\,634\times10^{-19}\ \mathrm{C}$, and this item does not assert that physical charge is quantised; the magnetic constant $\mu_0>0$ carries N A$^{-2}$ and is measured, so no exact numerical value of $\mu_0$ is asserted (the pre-2019 SI fixed the historical nominal $\mu_{0,\mathrm{nom}}:=4\pi\times10^{-7}\ \mathrm{H\,m^{-1}}=4\pi\times10^{-7}\ \mathrm{N\,A^{-2}}$ exactly; since the revised SI took effect on 20 May 2019, $\mu_0$ is experimentally determined. The SI brochure quotes the nominal $\mu_{0,\mathrm{nom}}$ as the estimate at the 2019 adoption with relative standard uncertainty $2.3\times10^{-10}$; this is historical estimate/uncertainty context, not an exact equality for the actual $\mu_0$ or a current measured value); the electric constant is defined within the framework by $\varepsilon_0:=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ in F m$^{-1}$, consistent with the exact SI relation $\varepsilon_0\mu_0=1/c^2$, so that $c^2\varepsilon_0\mu_0=1$ and $\varepsilon_0$ inherits the relative standard uncertainty of $\mu_0$. (b) [Electromagnetic quantities] Charge $q$ carries the coulomb (C); the charge density $\rho$ of [[def-em-sources]] carries C m$^{-3}$ and the current density $J$ carries A m$^{-2}$, so that the four-current components $(c\rho,J)$ carry A m$^{-2}$; the electric field $E$ carries V m$^{-1}$; the magnetic field $B$ carries the tesla (T), where $1\ \mathrm{T}=1\ \mathrm{N\,A^{-1}\,m^{-1}}$; the scalar potential $\varphi$ carries V and the vector potential $A$ carries T m, so that the four-potential components $(\varphi/c,A)$ carry T m; the components of the electromagnetic two-form of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] carry T; a force carries the newton (N), $1\ \mathrm{N}=1\ \mathrm{kg\,m\,s^{-2}}$. (c) [Mechanical quantities] A rest mass parameter $m$ carries the kilogram (kg) and a four-momentum $P=mU$ carries kg m s$^{-1}$ ([[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]]); field energy density carries J m$^{-3}$, energy flux W m$^{-2}$, so that $1\ \mathrm{W}=1\ \mathrm{J\,s^{-1}}=1\ \mathrm{V\,A}$. (d) [Bookkeeping only] The unit of a quantity records the adopted system of units; it does not show that a quantity is primitive in this or any other framework, it contains no measurement, and it does not identify a quantity with a similarly named quantity of another framework. The exact defining values of $c$ and $e$ fix numerical conventions of the SI, they do not by themselves identify $c$ with the vacuum propagation constant of ideal light, which is the physical adoption of [[post-em-minkowski-physical-model]].
dependency_ordered_snapshots.strategy: A convention definition: it fixes the coordinate normalisation $x^0=ct$, the unit of each quantity used in this framework, the exact SI defining values of $c$ and $e$ and the measured status of $\mu_0$. The exact values $c=299\,792\,458$ m/s and $e=1.602\,176\,634\times10^{-19}$ C, and the statements that the new definition of the ampere fixes $e$ rather than $\mu_0$, that $\mu_0$ must now be determined experimentally, and that $\varepsilon_0\mu_0=1/c^2$ remains exact, are taken from the SI brochure's defining-constants table and its ampere section. The framework's definition of $\varepsilon_0$ by $(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ is a definition consistent with that exact relation; the uncertainty carried by $\varepsilon_0$ is recorded rather than hidden. The dimensional checks of the framework's equations and couplings are developed on the companion examples page of this pair. No exact or current measured numerical value of $\mu_0$ is asserted and no experiment is claimed. The historical nominal and adoption uncertainty are explicitly source context, not a substitution for the current experimentally determined constant.
dependency_ordered_snapshots.focused_actual_supplier_use_review: Verified current exact c/e and positive measured mu0; historical nominal/adoption uncertainty remains contextual, not current equality.

dependency_ordered_snapshots.statement: Let the laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$, its spatial Euclidean structure and its units be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] and [[def-em-si-conventions]], and let $k\ge1$. An electric field of class $C^k$ on the region is a map $E:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ that is of class $C^k$ in the sense of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]; a magnetic field of class $C^k$ is a map $B:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ of the same class. At fixed $t\in I$ the maps $E(\cdot,t),B(\cdot,t):\Omega\to\mathbb R^3$ are real spatial vector fields on the region $\Omega$, read in the $\delta$-orthonormal basis $(e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of the frame. The framework uses: $C^1$ fields in the classical Maxwell branch, $C^2$ fields where second or mixed time-space derivatives of the fields appear, and $C^\infty$ fields in the smooth existence branches; every statement carries its own regularity and no regularity beyond it is asserted. Conventions: (a) $E$ is a polar vector and $B$ an axial vector relative to the orientation of the spatial basis; the changes of inertial description adopted in [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]] are proper and orientation preserving, so orientation-reversing descriptions are not among them; (b) the fields are defined by their values on $\Omega\times I$, and no value at a point of singular source support is asserted; (c) $E$ carries V m$^{-1}$ and $B$ carries T; (d) the identification of the pair $(E,B)$ with the components of an alternating two-form, including its transformation behaviour, is made in [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] and is not presupposed here.
dependency_ordered_snapshots.strategy: An explicit type/domain/convention definition: the fields are maps on the product $\Omega\times I$ of the laboratory region with a stated class of regularity, and their fixed-time readings are spatial vector fields in the frame basis. The regularity notion is that of [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]; the polar/axial convention and the exclusion of pointwise values at singular source support are conventions recorded explicitly rather than used implicitly. No differential equation and no derived quantity is introduced by this definition.
dependency_ordered_snapshots.focused_actual_supplier_use_review: Unchanged Ck domain/type and SI units remain applicable; field definition uses no nominal mu0 numerical value or rest-density assumption.
dependency_ordered_snapshots.disposition: unchanged claim/strategy reviewed against changed actual interfaces

dependency_ordered_snapshots.statement: Adopt as physical assumptions of this framework: (i) the oriented time-oriented affine Minkowski space $(A,V,\eta,C^+)$ of the mathematical model [[def-em-minkowski-affine-space]], together with the conversion constant $c>0$ of [[def-em-si-conventions]], is the spacetime of the framework: its points represent idealized physical events, displacements represent idealized spacetime separations, and the causal classification of the model is the framework's causal structure; (ii) the inertial frames and charts of [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]] are the inertial descriptions of the framework, and changes of description are the proper orthochronous isometries adopted in [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]]; (iii) the ideal clock reading rule along future timelike curves and the identification of ideal vacuum light rays with future null straight lines, both with the same constant $c$, are those adopted in [[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]]; (iv) the laboratory description of fields and sources is the restricted inertial chart of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], with the spatial Euclidean structure and the SI conventions of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] and [[def-em-si-conventions]]. Status and scope: the mathematical model defines the geometry and its theorems prove geometric facts only; that physical events are described by the model, that ideal clocks read the stated proper time and that ideal vacuum light follows null straight lines are adopted assumptions, not deductions from experiment or from the mathematical axioms. The special-relativity postulates adopted here do not by themselves select the Maxwell equations, a force law or any matter model: the electromagnetic equations and couplings of this framework are further postulates of it. The framework is classical, flat and non-quantum; gravitational curvature, quantum fields and measurement postulates are outside its scope.
dependency_ordered_snapshots.strategy: A postulate, not a theorem: it records the adopted physical reading of the mathematical Minkowski model of [[def-em-minkowski-affine-space]] and reuses the two special-relativity physical postulates [[post-sr-inertial-covariance]] and [[post-sr-ideal-clocks-and-light]] with the shared constant $c$ as the vacuum propagation constant. The exposition must separate what the mathematical model fixes (the affine geometry, its causal cones, its frames) from what is adopted (the event interpretation, the clock and light interpretation, the inertial-description equivalence). It must also state that Maxwell's equations and the Lorentz coupling are additional postulates not implied by the SR assumptions, and it asserts no empirical measurement or verification.
dependency_ordered_snapshots.focused_actual_supplier_use_review: Unchanged adopted spacetime/light/clock physical reading uses exact SI c; no source-density integral or empirical mu0 equality is deduced.
dependency_ordered_snapshots.disposition: unchanged claim/strategy reviewed against changed actual interfaces

dependency_ordered_snapshots.statement: The particle and light objects of the framework are the following curves and vector fields of the affine Minkowski model ([[def-sr-affine-minkowski-model]], [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]), with the physical interpretation of [[post-em-minkowski-physical-model]] and the units of [[def-em-si-conventions]]. (a) [Worldlines] A worldline is a regular causal curve $x:J\to A$ in one of the regularity classes of [[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]] ($J$ an order-convex subset of $\mathbb R$ with at least two elements). A massive worldline is a $C^k$ future timelike worldline, $k\ge1$, with everywhere nonzero future timelike tangent; a light ray is a $C^1$ future null curve with everywhere nonzero future null tangent. A null curve has zero proper-time increment along every subinterval and no proper-time parametrization ([[def-sr-proper-time]]), and it is never treated as a massive worldline. A worldline is a curve in spacetime; its reading $r\circ x$ in a named laboratory chart is a coordinate description of it, not an object of another observer. (b) [Four-velocity and four-acceleration] For a massive worldline the four-velocity $U$ and, when it is $C^2$, the four-acceleration $A$ are those of [[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]]; wherever defined they satisfy $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$ and $\eta(U,A)=0$, by [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]. (c) [Chart reading] If a massive $C^2$ worldline has laboratory reading $t\mapsto r(t)$ in a chart of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], then $|r'(t)|<c$ for every $t$, with four-velocity $U=\gamma(c,r')$ and Lorentz factor $\gamma=(1-|r'|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$, by clause (e) of [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]. (d) [Frames and observers] An inertial frame in this framework is the origin-with-basis object of [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]]; a point observer is a future unit timelike vector $n\in V$ with rest space $n^\perp$ and rest projection $h$, as in clauses (c)-(d) of [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]. An observer congruence and a noninertial tetrad field are further objects, not defined by this item; the words 'frame', 'chart', 'observer' and 'tetrad' denote distinct notions and are not interchangeable. (e) [Scope] No force law, no self-field and no extended-body structure is supplied here; an accelerating massive worldline requires a force model stated separately, and an ideal light ray carries no dispersive, quantum or polarisation structure in this definition.
dependency_ordered_snapshots.strategy: A definition reusing the special-relativity curve notions with their exact statements rather than restating them: regularity and causal character of curves are those of [[def-sr-regular-causal-curve-and-worldline]]; proper time and its non-applicability to null curves are those of [[def-sr-proper-time]]; $U$ and $A$ are those of [[def-sr-four-velocity-and-four-acceleration]]; the identities $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$, $\eta(U,A)=0$, the chart bound $|r'|<c$ and the velocity reading $U=\gamma(c,r')$ are the exact clauses of [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]. The frame/observer distinction is the one of [[def-inertial-frame-and-inertial-chart]] together with the rest-space and projection clauses of the same theorem. The item adds the physical interpretation adopted in [[post-em-minkowski-physical-model]] and records the scope exclusions; it proves no dynamical statement.
dependency_ordered_snapshots.focused_actual_supplier_use_review: Unchanged proper-time U normalization and causal/frame conventions supply exactly the additional normalized material branch; no arbitrary timelike U is silently normalized.
dependency_ordered_snapshots.disposition: unchanged claim/strategy reviewed against changed actual interfaces

dependency_ordered_snapshots.statement:
Let the laboratory region and its chart be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], with the units of [[def-em-si-conventions]]. (a) [Charge parameter] The framework takes a real charge parameter $q\in\mathbb R$, measured in coulombs, attached to a source; its sign is the sign of the source and it is a parameter of the model. Charge quantisation is not asserted. (b) [Smooth source fields] A smooth (volume) source field on $\Omega\times I$ is a pair $(\rho,J)$ of maps $\rho:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R$, $J:\Omega\times I\to\mathbb R^3$ that is continuous on $\Omega\times I$ and of class $C^1$ wherever a displayed equation differentiates it; $\rho$ is the frame charge density (C m$^{-3}$) and $J$ the frame current density (A m$^{-2}$). For each fixed $t\in I$ retain the compact Jordan branch: if $V\subseteq\Omega$ is compact and Jordan measurable, define $Q_R(V,t):=\int_V\rho(y,t)dy$ by [[def-riemann-integral-over-a-jordan-set]], with integrability supplied by [[thm-continuous-functions-on-compact-jordan-sets-are-integrable]]. For the full measurable-volume branch assume Countable Choice ([[def-countable-choice]]), as required by the published Lebesgue-measure interface. If $V$ is any bounded Lebesgue-measurable subset with compact closure $\overline V\subseteq\Omega$, define
$$Q(V,t):=\int_V\rho(y,t)d\lambda_3(y)=\int_{\mathbb R^3}F_t(y)\mathbf1_V(y)d\lambda_3(y),$$
where $F_t=\rho(\cdot,t)$ on $\Omega$ and $0$ elsewhere; the signed integral is defined through its positive and negative parts ([[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]], [[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]]). This integral is absolutely finite, since $\rho(\cdot,t)$ is bounded on $\overline V$ and $V$ has finite Lebesgue measure. On the compact Jordan branch, under the same Countable Choice assumption, $Q=Q_R$ by [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]]. The empty region has charge zero in both branches. The current flux remains defined independently: for each oriented surface patch in $\Omega$ with unit normal field $n_S$ the current flux at time $t$ is $\int_S J(y,t)\cdot n_S(y)\,dS$ ([[def-oriented-unit-normal-and-flux-of-a-surface-patch]]). Point sources and sheet sources are not source fields in this sense; they are different objects, defined by their own pairings when the framework uses them. (c) [Covariant identification] Write $j:=(c\rho,J)$, so $j^0=c\rho$ and $j^i=J^i$. The framework adopts as a model premise the identification of the charge-current of a source with a vector field of the affine Minkowski model, and hence the component transformation law of [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]] for $j$ between inertial charts. This is a model premise, not a theorem about physical currents. (d) [Frame density, scalar multiplier and the normalized material branch] Suppose additionally that the identified $j$ is $C^1$ and $j=\rho_0U$, with a $C^1$ future timelike vector field $U$ and a $C^1$ real scalar multiplier $\rho_0$. Since $U^0>0$, define the normalized chart direction $u:=U/U^0$, so $u^0=1$, $u^i=U^i/U^0$. Then $j=(\rho_0U^0)u$ and, because the electromagnetic convention is $j^0=c\rho$,
$$\rho=\rho_0U^0/c,\qquad J^i=\rho_0U^i=c\rho\,u^i.$$
Pointwise equality $\rho=\rho_0$ holds if and only if $\rho_0(U^0-c)=0$, including the zero-multiplier case. Where $\rho_0\ne0$, equality is equivalent to $U^0=c$, which does not alone imply $U^i=0$ for an arbitrary future timelike $U$. Thus a scalar multiplier is not automatically a Lorentz rest charge density. The direction $u$ is chart normalized, with no unit or proper-four-velocity normalization imposed in this general branch; if its coordinate velocity interpretation is adopted, the spatial velocity is $v^i:=cu^i$.
For the separate convective source model, explicitly assume that $U$ is the material proper-time four-velocity, normalized by $\eta(U,U)=-c^2$ as in [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]. This is an additional model condition, not a consequence of the factorization $j=\rho_0U$. In that branch, $U=\gamma(c,v)$, $|v|<c$, $\gamma=(1-|v|^2/c^2)^{-1/2}$, and
$$\rho=\gamma\rho_0,\qquad J=\rho v.$$
Here $\rho_0$ is the rest charge density of this stipulated convective model: in a comoving inertial frame $U=(c,0,0,0)$ and $j=(c\rho_0,0,0,0)$. The equality $\rho=\rho_0$ then holds exactly where $\rho_0=0$ or $v=0$ (equivalently $\gamma=1$). Both signs of charge and the zero-density case are retained. (e) [Scope] This definition fixes the source objects of the smooth branch and their transformation interface. It asserts no conservation law (that is proved for stated source classes) and no regularity of singular sources.
dependency_ordered_snapshots.strategy:
Keep clauses (a)-(c) as explicit source types and the adopted physical identification. The compact Jordan branch uses [[thm-continuous-functions-on-compact-jordan-sets-are-integrable]] and [[def-riemann-integral-over-a-jordan-set]]; flux uses [[def-oriented-unit-normal-and-flux-of-a-surface-patch]]. For the broader Lebesgue branch assume the explicitly stated Countable Choice, without Dependent Choice or a convergence/FTC assumption. Fix $t$ and an admitted nonempty $V$. The continuous function $\rho(\cdot,t)$ is bounded by $M_t<\infty$ in absolute value on compact $\overline V$ by [[thm-extreme-value-metric]]. Its zero extension $F_t$ is Borel: for every open $O\subseteq\mathbb R$, the inverse image inside the open set $\Omega$ is relatively open and hence open in $\mathbb R^3$; add the closed complement of $\Omega$ precisely when $0\in O$. This is also the open-set form of [[thm-continuous-preimages-of-borel-sets-are-borel]]. Under Countable Choice, Borel sets are Lebesgue measurable ([[thm-borel-sets-are-lebesgue-measurable]]) and bounded measurable $V$ has finite measure ([[prop-lebesgue-measure-is-sigma-finite-and-finite-on-bounded-sets]]). Positive/negative parts and their restrictions by $\mathbf1_V$ are measurable by [[prop-closure-properties-of-measurable-functions-used-by-the-integral]]. The bound $|F_t|\mathbf1_V\le M_t\mathbf1_V$ and [[prop-order-and-scalar-rules-for-the-nonnegative-integral]] give
$$\int|F_t|\mathbf1_Vd\lambda_3\le M_t\lambda_3(V)<\infty,$$
where the indicator integral is its simple-function value by [[prop-the-nonnegative-integral-agrees-with-the-simple-integral]]. This proves exactly the absolute signed integrability required by [[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]] and defines $Q$ using the nonnegative restrictions of [[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]]. For empty $V$ the product is zero. On compact Jordan $V$, the continuous density restricted to V has a bounded Borel zero extension to a bounding rectangle, so the exact compact-Jordan clause of [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]], also under Countable Choice, identifies the two finite integral values. The algebraic supplier [[thm-sr-tensor-and-current-transformation]](vii) gives $j=\rho_0U=\rho_0U^0u$; its coordinate density is $j^0$, whereas the present SI source convention defines $j^0=c\rho$. Division by $c>0$ gives $\rho=\rho_0U^0/c$ and $\rho-\rho_0=\rho_0(U^0-c)/c$, proving exactly the stated equality cases. The spatial components give $J^i=c\rho u^i$. Neither $U^0=c$ nor chart normalization $u^0=1$ is a proper-four-velocity condition.
In the additional normalized material model, write $v=c(U^1,U^2,U^3)/U^0$. The norm equation $-(U^0)^2+|U_{\mathrm{sp}}|^2=-c^2$ gives $(U^0)^2(1-|v|^2/c^2)=c^2$, and future timelikeness gives $U^0>0$ and $|v|<c$, so $U^0=c\gamma$. This is the exact four-velocity/relative-velocity content of [[thm-sr-proper-time-and-observer-decomposition]]; substitution gives $\rho=\gamma\rho_0$ and $J=\rho v$. In its comoving frame $U^0=c$, hence the source convention identifies the scalar multiplier with the stipulated rest-frame density. Since $\gamma=1$ if and only if $v=0$, the normalized equality cases follow, including $\rho_0=0$. All density readings remain within the adopted current model; no conservation, measurement, general current factorization, force law or singular-source regularity is deduced.
dependency_ordered_snapshots.focused_actual_supplier_use_review: Verified both volume branches, AComega only on declared Lebesgue interface, finite absolute integral and compact-Jordan comparison; general multiplier and normalized rest branch retain distinct conditions.

Let the laboratory region, its inertial chart and the fields and sources be those of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], [[def-em-fields]] and [[def-em-sources]], with the units of [[def-em-si-conventions]]; fix the ordered basis $(e_0,e_1,e_2,e_3)$ of the chart and the oriented volume form $\varepsilon$ of [[def-oriented-minkowski-volume-form]], with $\varepsilon_{0123}=+1$ and $\eta=\operatorname{diag}(-1,1,1,1)$. (a) [Components] For a field pair $(E,B)$ of class $C^k$, $k\ge1$, define the covariant components of the electromagnetic two-form $F$ in the chart by $F_{00}=0$, $F_{0i}:=-E_i/c$, $F_{ij}:=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$ ($i,j,k\in\{1,2,3\}$) and $F_{ab}:=-F_{ba}$, the index-raised components being $F^{0i}=E_i/c$, $F^{i0}=-E_i/c$ and $F^{ij}=\epsilon_{ijk}B_k$. dependency_ordered_snapshots.strategy:
An explicit definition computed from the components. The components $F_{ab}$ of clause (a) are $C^k$ functions of the inertial coordinates, because they are built from the $C^k$ functions $E_i,B_k$ and the constants $c,\epsilon_{ijk}$; hence $F$ is a $C^k$ tensor field by the component criterion of [[def-ck-tensor-field-on-minkowski-space]], and it is alternating because $F_{ab}=-F_{ba}$ by construction. Clause (b) is a direct substitution into clauses (a)-(c) of [[thm-sr-antisymmetric-observer-decomposition]] with $n=e_0$: $e_i=F_{i0}=+E_i/c$, $b_i=-	frac12\epsilon_{ijk}F_{jk}=-B_i$, the invariants $	frac12F_{ab}F^{ab}=|b|^2-|e|^2$ and $F_{ab}(*F)^{ab}=-4\,e\cdot b$ are evaluated with these values, and the square wedge uses the theorem's normalisation $F\wedge F=2\,(e\cdot b)\,\varepsilon$. For the same E,B, the optional tensor in the supplier is the negative of the entire adopted tensor; no magnetic-only sign conversion is used. This is the complete weak mixed-derivative cancellation using compact Riemann test identities, with no choice assumption and no narrowing to $C^2$ potentials. The spatial curl/gradient dictionary is the exact coordinate definition [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] at fixed time. Clause (d) restates the raised-index operator of [[lem-em-antisymmetric-tensor-contraction]] and the units of [[def-em-si-conventions]]. No physical law is proved and no empirical claim is made.

dependency_ordered_snapshots.statement:
Adopt as a physical postulate of this framework the following four equations for the fields of [[def-em-fields]] and the sources of [[def-em-sources]] on the laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$ of [[def-em-lab-geometry]], with $\mu_0>0$, $c>0$, $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ and the SI units of [[def-em-si-conventions]]. (a) [Smooth branch] Let $E,B$ be jointly $C^1$ fields with the additional derivatives required by each equation existing and continuous, and let $\rho,J$ be continuous. Then, with the divergence and curl of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] and the partial derivative $\partial_t$ at fixed position of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]],

$$\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0,\qquad \operatorname{div}B=0,\qquad \operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB,\qquad \operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE.$$

(b) [Weak branch] Let instead $E,B$ be locally integrable $\mathbb R^3$-valued fields and $\rho,J$ locally integrable scalar and vector fields on $I\times\Omega$, identified with their regular distributions ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]], [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]]). Let $\operatorname{div}$, $\operatorname{curl}$ and $\partial_t$ act as distributional derivatives, and let $\psi$ range over $C_c^\infty(I\times\Omega)$ ([[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]]). Then the same four identities hold in the sense of [[def-distribution]]: the pairings $\langle\operatorname{div}E-\rho/\varepsilon_0,\psi\rangle$, $\langle\operatorname{div}B,\psi\rangle$, $\langle\operatorname{curl}E+\partial_tB,\psi\rangle$ and $\langle\operatorname{curl}B-\mu_0J-c^{-2}\partial_tE,\psi\rangle$ vanish for every such $\psi$, all derivatives being distributional derivatives ([[def-distributional-derivative]]). (c) [Scope] The postulate contains no magnetic charge: $\operatorname{div}B=0$ and no magnetic-source term appears in $\operatorname{curl}E$. Sources that are not locally integrable functions (point or sheet sources) are covered by neither branch and require their own definition. The equations are adopted classical vacuum physics in the named inertial chart; they are not deduced from charge conservation, from empirical agreement or from the special-relativity postulates, and this item by itself asserts no covariance under changes of inertial frame.
dependency_ordered_snapshots.strategy: A postulate, not a theorem. Obligations and conventions: the fields and sources are those of [[def-em-fields]] and [[def-em-sources]], the operators are the published divergence and curl of [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]] and the partial derivative of [[def-directional-and-partial-derivatives]], and the weak reading uses exactly the regular-distribution embedding, the test space and the distributional derivative named in the statement. The exposition must state that the four equations are adopted, that the choice of the sign and constant conventions is the one fixed by [[def-em-si-conventions]], and that no magnetic charge is included; the sources not covered by either branch are excluded explicitly. Empirical support for Maxwell's equations is a nonlogical relation of the framework, not a proof, and no verification is claimed here.

Delta sources still require future separate weak-source adoption. No volume-charge integral is used to deduce Maxwell equations.

dependency_ordered_snapshots.statement: This example is conditional on the definitions [[def-em-sources]], [[def-em-fields]] and the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]], and assumes Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ both for the Lebesgue-volume source branch and for the injectivity of the regular-distribution embedding used below ([[def-countable-choice]]). (a) [Smooth source] Let $f\in C_c^\infty(\mathbb R^3)$ be nonnegative with Lebesgue normalization $\int_{\mathbb R^3}f\,d\lambda_3=1$ (the Riemann integral over any compact box containing $\operatorname{supp}f$ has the same value by [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]]) (for instance any nonzero nonnegative smooth compactly supported bump divided by its finite nonzero integral), let $q\in\mathbb R$, and let $\Omega\subseteq\mathbb R^3$ be a nonempty open set containing $\operatorname{supp}f$. Then $\rho:=qf$ and $J:=0$ is a smooth source field of [[def-em-sources]]: $\rho$ is compactly supported and of class $C^\infty$, hence continuous, and for every bounded Lebesgue-measurable $V$ with compact closure inside $\Omega$ and containing $\operatorname{supp}f$, the charge is $Q(V,t)=q\int f=q$; the same value holds for the retained compact Jordan/Riemann branch at every time $t$, so the smooth branch of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] applies to this source. (b) [Point source] Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open interval and $z:I\to\mathbb R^3$ a $C^1$ trajectory whose graph map $t\mapsto(z(t),t)$ is proper into $\Omega\times I$ ([[lem-em-point-current-continuity]]; properness is automatic when $\Omega\times I$ is the whole ambient domain or when $I=\mathbb R$). For $q\in\mathbb R$, the pairings $\langle\rho,\psi\rangle:=q\int_I\psi(z(t),t)\,dt$ and $\langle J,\psi\rangle:=q\int_Iz'(t)\psi(z(t),t)\,dt$, for $\psi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega\times I)$, are the point-source distributions of [[lem-em-point-current-continuity]]: they are distributions ([[def-distribution]], [[def-test-function-space-d-of-an-open-set]]) satisfying $\partial_t\rho+\operatorname{div}J=0$ in the distributional sense. At each fixed time $t$ this model assigns the charge $q\cdot\mathbf 1_{z(t)\in V}$ to a Jordan-measurable $V\subseteq\Omega$, and its instantaneous spatial density is the evaluation functional $q\delta_{z(t)}$ ([[def-dirac-delta-and-its-derivatives]]), $\varphi\mapsto q\,\varphi(z(t))$; a source field of the smooth branch instead gives the integrals $\varphi\mapsto\int_\Omega\rho(y,t)\varphi(y)\,dy$ of its continuous density. (c) [The two classes differ] Fix $t\in I$, put $z_0:=z(t)\in\Omega$ and suppose $q\ne0$. Assume the Axiom of Countable Choice AC_omega only as it is carried by [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]] in the argument below, through the injectivity of the regular-distribution map ([[def-countable-choice]]). Then no locally integrable $\rho\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$ represents the point charge: there is no such $\rho$ whose regular distribution ([[def-regular-distribution-from-a-locally-integrable-function]]) satisfies $\langle\rho,\varphi\rangle=q\,\varphi(z_0)$ for every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$. Indeed, if $\rho$ did, then on the open set $\Omega\setminus\{z_0\}$ every test vanishes at $z_0$, so the regular distribution of the restriction of $\rho$ is zero, and injectivity gives $\rho=0$ almost everywhere there ([[def-measure-null-set-and-almost-everywhere]]); since $\{z_0\}$ is Lebesgue-null ([[prop-countable-subsets-of-rn-are-lebesgue-null]]) and a union of two null sets is null ([[thm-finite-and-countable-subadditivity-of-measures]]), $\rho=0$ almost everywhere on $\Omega$. The regular distribution depends only on the almost-everywhere class, so $\langle\rho,\varphi_0\rangle=0$ for a cutoff $\varphi_0\in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$ with $\varphi_0=1$ near $z_0$ ([[lem-test-function-cutoffs-and-euclidean-localization]]), while the assumed identity gives $\langle\rho,\varphi_0\rangle=q\varphi_0(z_0)=q\ne0$: a contradiction. Hence the point source is not a source field of the smooth branch of [[def-em-sources]] (whose densities are continuous functions), and the smooth-branch equations are not applied to it pointwise; the point source enters the framework only through its distributional pairings. (d) [Conclusion] The two source classes carry the same parameter $q$ and the same total charge $q$ (the smooth density integrates to $q$; the point model assigns charge $q$ to regions containing the particle), but they are different mathematical objects with different regularity, and they enter the framework through different branches. This example asserts no field value at $z(t)$ and contains no measurement or empirical claim.
dependency_ordered_snapshots.strategy: For the smooth-source charge claim in (a), assume the declared Countable Choice. The continuous density $qf$ satisfies both source-volume branches of [[def-em-sources]]. For any admitted bounded Lebesgue-measurable $V$ containing $\operatorname{supp}f$, $f\mathbf1_V=f$ pointwise. Since $f\ge0$ and $\int f=1$, it is integrable, and [[thm-linearity-of-the-lebesgue-integral-on-l-one]] gives $Q(V,t)=\int_Vqf=q\int f=q$ through [[def-integrable-real-and-complex-functions-and-their-integrals]] and the positive/negative restrictions of [[def-integral-over-a-measurable-set]]. For compact Jordan $V$, [[lem-riemann-lebesgue-comparison-for-distribution-test-integrands]] identifies this value with the Riemann charge. No new convergence or differentiation result is needed. Direct computations and one short contradiction. (a) $\rho=qf$ is $C^\infty$ with compact support, hence continuous and bounded; for a compact Jordan-measurable $V$ containing the support, the integral of $\rho$ over $V$ equals $q\int f=q$ by the definition of $f$ and additivity of the integral over the support complement ([[def-riemann-integral-over-a-jordan-set]]). (b) The pairings and the continuity equation are exactly the content of [[lem-em-point-current-continuity]] under its properness hypothesis; the fixed-time reading $q\delta_{z(t)}$ is the evaluation functional of [[def-dirac-delta-and-its-derivatives]]. (c) Suppose $u_\rho=q\delta_{z_0}$ with $\rho\in L^1_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$. On the open set $\Omega\setminus\{z_0\}$, for every $\varphi\in C_c^\infty(\Omega\setminus\{z_0\})$ one has $u_\rho(\varphi)=q\varphi(z_0)=0$; the injectivity clause of [[thm-locally-integrable-functions-embed-in-distributions]], which carries AC_omega, gives $\rho=0$ almost everywhere on $\Omega\setminus\{z_0\}$. The singleton $\{z_0\}$ is null by [[prop-countable-subsets-of-rn-are-lebesgue-null]], and the union of the exceptional null set with $\{z_0\}$ is null by finite subadditivity ([[thm-finite-and-countable-subadditivity-of-measures]], [[def-measure-null-set-and-almost-everywhere]]), so $\rho=0$ almost everywhere on $\Omega$. By the definition of the regular distribution (which depends only on the almost-everywhere class) $u_\rho=0$, i.e. $u_\rho(\varphi)=0$ for every test. The cutoff lemma supplies $\varphi_0$ with $\varphi_0=1$ near $z_0$, and the assumed identity gives $u_\rho(\varphi_0)=q\varphi_0(z_0)=q\ne0$, a contradiction. (d) is the bookkeeping of the two total charges. No field equation is solved, no regularity of the point source is asserted beyond its distributional definition, and the only choice principle used is Countable Choice, carried explicitly both by the Lebesgue-volume/comparison branch and by the embedding theorem's injectivity.

dependency_ordered_snapshots.statement: Assume the vacuum Maxwell postulate [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] on the laboratory region $U\cong I\times\Omega$ of [[def-em-lab-geometry]] with the fields of [[def-em-fields]] and the sources of [[def-em-sources]], and fix the constants $\mu_0>0$, $c>0$, $\varepsilon_0=(\mu_0c^2)^{-1}$ of [[def-em-si-conventions]]. Let $n\ge1$, let $(E_1,B_1,\rho_1,J_1),\dots,(E_n,B_n,\rho_n,J_n)$ be $n$ field-source pairs each satisfying one and the same branch of the postulate on the same region (all in the smooth branch, or all in the weak branch), and let $a_1,\dots,a_n\in\mathbb R$. Put $E:=\sum_{j=1}^na_jE_j$, $B:=\sum_{j=1}^na_jB_j$, $\rho:=\sum_{j=1}^na_j\rho_j$ and $J:=\sum_{j=1}^na_jJ_j$. Then: (a) $(E,B,\rho,J)$ satisfies the same branch of the postulate on the same region with the same constants: pointwise in the smooth branch and in the sense of the pairings of clause (b) of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] in the weak branch. (b) Nothing beyond this linearity is asserted: the result does not apply to a source whose density depends nonlinearly on the fields (a nonlinear constitutive law), and no convergence statement is made for infinite series or integrals of solutions or for infinite linear combinations. (c) The theorem is conditional on the adopted postulate and is not an empirical claim about nature.
dependency_ordered_snapshots.strategy: **Proof technique:** direct termwise computation, smooth branch and distributional branch separately. In the smooth branch, the divergence and curl are linear in their arguments because they are finite sums of first partial derivatives ([[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]], [[thm-algebra-of-derivatives]]), and $\partial_t$ is linear likewise; hence $\operatorname{div}E=\sum_ja_j\operatorname{div}E_j=\sum_ja_j\rho_j/\varepsilon_0=\rho/\varepsilon_0$ and, in the same way, $\operatorname{div}B=0$, $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$ and $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$. In the weak branch the distributional derivatives are linear and the pairings are linear in the distributions ([[def-distribution]], [[def-distributional-derivative]]), so the four vanishing pairings of the postulate for the sum follow by summing the finitely many vanishing pairings of the summands with the same test function. The scope clauses (nonlinear sources, no infinite superposition) are recorded in the theorem itself; no physical premise beyond the postulate is used, and no empirical premise occurs, so no empirical qualifications are inherited beyond the postulate's own.

dependency_ordered_snapshots.statement:
Adopt as physical postulates of this framework, on the spacetime and particle model of [[post-em-minkowski-physical-model]] and [[def-em-relativistic-worldlines-frames]] and on the special-relativity particle model [[post-sr-massive-particle-dynamics]]: (i) [Test charge in a prescribed external field] Let $q\in\mathbb R$ be a constant charge parameter ([[def-em-sources]]), $m>0$ an externally supplied rest mass, $x:J\to A$ a future timelike $C^2$ massive worldline with four-velocity $U$, and let $F$ be a prescribed field of [[def-em-electromagnetic-tensor]] that is $C^1$ on a neighbourhood of the graph of $x$ and is generated externally to the particle. Adopt the equation of motion

$$m\,\frac{dU}{d\tau}=q\,\Phi(U),$$

where $\Phi$ is the raised-index operator of the field at the event $x(\tau)$, defined by $\eta(\Phi(u),w)=F(w,u)$ ([[lem-em-antisymmetric-tensor-contraction]]); equivalently $m\,dU^\mu/d\tau=q\,F^{\mu\nu}U_\nu$. The particle's own field is excluded from $F$: this is the external-field coupling, and it defines no self-force. (ii) [Continuum matter coupling] For a smooth source $(\rho,J)$ of [[def-em-sources]] interacting with the field through an explicitly stated matter model to which this coupling applies, adopt the force density $\rho E+J\times B$ (unit N m$^{-3}$) and the power density $J\cdot E$ (unit W m$^{-3}$) as the electromagnetic source terms of that matter model; they describe the local interaction of the field with matter and are not a property of a prescribed current alone. (iii) [Scope] The rest mass and the charge are inputs; $m$ is not derived within electromagnetism. The coupling is adopted for constant $q$ and $m>0$; no magnetic-monopole coupling, no radiation reaction and no self-force are included. In particular the nonrelativistic coordinate statement $mr''=q(E+r'\times B)$ is not adopted as exact: the adopted statement is the covariant one of clause (i), and any low-speed statement requires its own approximation hypotheses and error bounds.
dependency_ordered_snapshots.strategy: A postulate, not a theorem. The exposition must state the exact data (constant charge, externally supplied positive rest mass, future timelike C^2 worldline, prescribed external field C^1 near the graph), name the raised-index operator $\Phi$ with its defining identity and index form from [[lem-em-antisymmetric-tensor-contraction]] so that the equation is unambiguous, and state the exclusion of the particle's own field. Clause (ii) is a formulation premise for matter models, with its units fixed by [[def-em-si-conventions]] and its cross product the spatial one of [[def-cross-product-in-r3]]; it is not a derivation from the field equations. Clause (iii) records the scope: no self-force, no radiation reaction, no magnetic monopole, and no exact Newtonian law. Empirical support for the coupling is a nonlogical relation of the framework; the item claims no verification and no measured value.

dependency_ordered_snapshots.statement: This example is conditional on the units of [[def-em-si-conventions]], the definitions of divergence and curl in [[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]], the equations of [[post-em-vacuum-maxwell]] and the coupling of [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]]; all equalities below are equalities of units, using $1\ \mathrm{C}=1\ \mathrm{A\,s}$, $1\ \mathrm{V}=1\ \mathrm{J\,C^{-1}}$, $1\ \mathrm{J}=1\ \mathrm{N\,m}$, $1\ \mathrm{W}=1\ \mathrm{V\,A}=1\ \mathrm{J\,s^{-1}}$, $1\ \mathrm{F}=1\ \mathrm{C\,V^{-1}}$ and $1\ \mathrm{T}=1\ \mathrm{N\,A^{-1}\,m^{-1}}$. (a) $\operatorname{div}E$ has unit $\mathrm{V\,m^{-2}}$ and $\rho/\varepsilon_0$ has unit $\mathrm{C\,m^{-3}/(F\,m^{-1})}=\mathrm{C\,V\,m^{-2}\,C^{-1}}=\mathrm{V\,m^{-2}}$, so the two sides of $\operatorname{div}E=\rho/\varepsilon_0$ agree. (b) $\operatorname{curl}B$ has unit $\mathrm{T\,m^{-1}}$; $\mu_0J$ has unit $\mathrm{N\,A^{-2}\cdot A\,m^{-2}}=\mathrm{N\,A^{-1}\,m^{-2}}=\mathrm{T\,m^{-1}}$; $c^{-2}\partial_tE$ has unit $\mathrm{m^{-2}\,s^{2}\cdot V\,m^{-1}\,s^{-1}}=\mathrm{V\,s\,m^{-3}}=\mathrm{N\,A^{-1}\,m^{-2}}=\mathrm{T\,m^{-1}}$, so both source terms of $\operatorname{curl}B=\mu_0J+c^{-2}\partial_tE$ have the unit of $\operatorname{curl}B$. (c) $\operatorname{curl}E$ has unit $\mathrm{V\,m^{-2}}=\mathrm{T\,s^{-1}}$ and $\partial_tB$ has unit $\mathrm{T\,s^{-1}}$, so $\operatorname{curl}E=-\partial_tB$ is homogeneous; $\operatorname{div}B=0$ is a homogeneous equation. (d) In the coupling of [[post-em-lorentz-coupling]], $qE$ has unit $\mathrm{C\cdot V\,m^{-1}}=\mathrm{J\,m^{-1}}=\mathrm{N}$ and $q\,(r'\times B)$ has unit $\mathrm{C\,m\,s^{-1}\,T}=\mathrm{C\,N\,A^{-1}\,s^{-1}}=\mathrm{N}$, so the two force terms add with the unit of a force; and $\rho E+J\times B$ has unit $\mathrm{C\,m^{-3}\,V\,m^{-1}}=\mathrm{N\,m^{-3}}$, the unit of a force density. (e) The energy density $\tfrac12(\varepsilon_0E^2+B^2/\mu_0)$ has unit $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$ and the flux $E\times B/\mu_0$ has unit $\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$, consistent with $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}\cdot m\,s^{-1}}=\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$. (f) The check is exact arithmetic of the adopted units; it is not a measurement, it does not prove the equations, and no numerical value of $\mu_0$ is used or asserted.
dependency_ordered_snapshots.strategy: Direct substitution in the unit table of [[def-em-si-conventions]]: each displayed unit computation is a product and quotient of the base and derived units listed there, with the conversion identities $1\ \mathrm{C}=1\ \mathrm{A\,s}$, $1\ \mathrm{V}=1\ \mathrm{J\,C^{-1}}$, $1\ \mathrm{J}=1\ \mathrm{N\,m}$ and $1\ \mathrm{T}=1\ \mathrm{N\,A^{-1}\,m^{-1}}$ quoted from the same source. The only structural input is that divergence divides a field unit by a length and curl does the same while preserving the field unit ([[def-divergence-and-curl-of-a-c1-vector-field]]); time derivatives divide by a time. All computations are finite and exact, and no empirical premise or measurement is used.
